story_type: night launch of the last Moon mission, then the last Moon walk, historic film
hook: The last ride to the Moon left in the dark.
narration: The last flight to the Moon lifted off at night.
It was Apollo 17, and even the hardened veterans of the space program felt the awe as it climbed.
The flame was so bright it lit the clouds and turned the dark sky over the pad orange.
On the Moon, geologist Harrison Schmitt stepped out into a magnificent valley.
He saw rolling hills, blocky fields of rocks around large craters, and bright mountain slopes rising in the distance.
outcome: Apollo 17 was the last time anyone walked on the Moon, and the crew left it in late 1972.
title: Apollo 17 launched at night
question_comment: Would you have wanted a seat on the last flight to the Moon?

facts.claim: Apollo 17 launched at night, veterans felt the awe
facts.source_quote: Apollo 17 was launched at night, and even the old hands, the hardened veterans of the space program couldn't help but feel the awe of the world.

facts.claim: Last flight to the Moon, last time man walked on its surface
facts.source_quote: When Apollo 17 was making its descent, the last flight to the moon, the last time that man walked on its surface, Schmitt remembers how it was.
Harrison Schmitt, doctor Harrison Schmitt, a geologist, he touched the moon and remembers how it was.

facts.claim: Valley, blocky fields of rocks, craters, bright slopes
facts.source_quote: The blocky fields of rocks that you know because you've studied the photographs, and you saw them as you descended, surround large craters that have been formed in that rolling countryside.
They last left there in late 1972.

description:
Apollo 17, the last flight to the Moon, lifts off at night from Kennedy Space Center in 1972, and geologist Harrison Schmitt explores a valley on the lunar surface.
